epics.description: Customers can export their paid orders as a CSV file from their account page. The export contains one row per order with order number, date and total amount including VAT, excludes cancelled orders, and uses the file name orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv. The delimiter and encoding of the file are not decided yet.

features.description: Capability for a customer to download a CSV file listing their paid, non-cancelled orders from the account page.
features.name: Order export

acceptanceCriteria: Given a logged-in customer on the account page, When the customer triggers the export, Then a CSV file containing their paid orders is downloaded.
Given the export is produced, When the file is opened, Then it is a CSV file whose delimiter and encoding follow the decision still pending from the Product Owner.
stories.aiReadyReason: The meaning of "paid" is undefined and the CSV delimiter and encoding are still pending, so the developer cannot decide which orders are exported or how the file is formatted. Question for the PO: What exactly makes an order "paid", and which delimiter (comma or semicolon) and encoding should the CSV use?
stories.description: A download action on the account page produces a CSV file containing the customer's paid orders. The delimiter (comma or semicolon) and the encoding of the file are not decided yet and must not be assumed. The meaning of paid is not defined in the specification.
stories.iWant: to download my paid orders as a CSV file from my account page
stories.soThat: I can keep a record of my orders outside the website
stories.title: Download paid orders as CSV from account page

acceptanceCriteria: Given a customer with two paid orders, When the export is produced, Then the file contains exactly two rows, one per order.
Given an exported order, When its row is read, Then it contains the order number, the order date and the total amount including VAT.
stories.aiReadyReason: The row content depends on the undefined business term "paid" used in the criteria, which changes which orders appear in the file. Question for the PO: What exactly makes an order "paid" so that the correct orders become rows?
dependencies: Download paid orders as CSV from account page
stories.description: The CSV file contains exactly one row per order, with the order number, the order date and the total amount including VAT. The format of the date value is left to the developer, as it does not change the information provided.
stories.iWant: each exported order to appear as one row with its order number, date and total amount including VAT
stories.soThat: I can review my order history in a spreadsheet
stories.title: Export one row per order with number, date and VAT-inclusive total

acceptanceCriteria: Given a customer with one paid order and one cancelled order, When the export is produced, Then the file contains only the paid order.
Given a customer whose orders are all cancelled, When the export is produced, Then the file contains no order rows.
stories.aiReadyReason: The exclusion rule is clear: orders with a cancelled status are left out of the file, and both criteria can be verified by setting up one paid and one cancelled order and checking the output.
dependencies: Export one row per order with number, date and VAT-inclusive total
stories.description: Orders with a cancelled status are not included in the exported CSV file.
stories.iWant: cancelled orders to be left out of my export
stories.soThat: the file only lists orders that are still valid

tasks.description: Update the export data retrieval so that orders with a cancelled status are excluded before the CSV is generated. Expected result: the export input contains only non-cancelled orders, and every other order field is unchanged.
tasks.title: Filter cancelled orders out of the export query

tasks.description: Write automated tests covering both acceptance criteria: a customer with one paid and one cancelled order yields a file with only the paid order row, and a customer whose orders are all cancelled yields a file with no order rows. Expected result: both tests pass.
tasks.title: Verify export excludes cancelled orders

stories.title: Exclude cancelled orders from export

acceptanceCriteria: Given a customer triggers the export, When the file is downloaded, Then its name follows the pattern orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv.
Given the file name is produced, When the date part is checked, Then it is a date in the YYYY-MM-DD format.
stories.aiReadyReason: The date in the file name is not defined, so the developer cannot know which date to use (export date, download date or another date) and the output value would be a business choice. Question for the PO: Which date should the YYYY-MM-DD part of the file name represent?
dependencies: Download paid orders as CSV from account page
stories.description: The downloaded file name follows the pattern orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv. The specification does not state which date the YYYY-MM-DD part represents.
stories.iWant: the exported file to be named orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv
stories.soThat: I can easily identify the export file by its date
stories.title: Name the exported file with its date
